caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1527 of 2006.
lawyer:
Md Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, Senior Advocate, instructed by Md Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record---For the Petitioner. 
Md Ibrahim Khalil, Advocate-on-Record---For Respondent No. 1. 
Not represented---Respondent No. 2.
parties:
Abu Taher ------ Petitioner
vs
Bangladesh ------ Respondents
full_judgment: 2. Facts, in brief, are that the petitioner filed the above writ petition on the averments that Abdus Salam became owner of the case property in terms of the registered lease agreement dated 11-2-1960 and he, by constructing building therein had been possessing the case property and he died on 16-1-1973 leaving behind Jebunnessa, his wife, two minor sons and four minor daughters; then Jebunnessa as guardian of the above minor children on obtaining necessary permission from the Court sold the case property to the petitioner by executing kabala dated 9-4-1973 on behalf of herself and the above minors and since then petitioner has been possessing the case property on mutating her name and paying rent, electric bills, WASA bills, gas bills, ground tax etc. and her name has also been recorded in the recent. Khatian and no notice for surrendering possession was ever issued by the Government to late Mr Abdus Salam or his heirs or to the petitioner as required for inclusion of the case property in the Kha list under Ordinance LIV of 1985. The respondent No. 1 contested the case but though did not file any written statement but their learned Advocate made oral submissions to the effect that the property has been rightly included in the list of abandoned buildings. The Court of Settlement, after hearing, allowed the case excluding the property from the list of abandoned buildings holding that the Government did not submit any office file to justify the inclusion of the case property in the list of abandoned buildings and, on the other hand, the petitioner filed original lease agreement, death certificate of Abdus Salam issued by the Secretary, Graveyard Committee, section 10 Mirpur, guardianship certificate dated 2-3-1973 issued in favour of Jebunnessa on the basis of which she sold the case property and also kabala dated 9-4-1973 by which the petitioner purchased the case property and those amply proved that Government illegally included the case property in the list of abandoned buildings. Then, after expiry of about eight years, the respondent No. 1 filed writ petition challenging the above judgment and order stating, inter alia, that the case property being an abandoned property vested in the government by operation of law and the petitioner completely failed to establish her claim in the case property and further, the case property was not also sold by its original owner with the prior permission of the government and that the plaintiff also did not file his nationality certificate to the Court of Settlement and further, on 6-3-1986 notice was duly issued upon the occupier of the case property but nobody turned up to raise objection in respect of inclusion of the case property in the list of abandoned buildings and the Court of Settlement also failed to apply his judicial mind to consider the relevant provisions of President's Order 16 of 1972 and Ordinance LIV of 1985.
